evidence.observation: The model-metadata lookup component. It pins the upstream litellm metadata URL (model_prices_and_context_window.json) and a 24h CACHE_TTL (lines 162-166), and in __init__ resolves a local on-disk cache at ~/.aider/caches/model_prices_and_context_window.json plus an in-memory local_model_metadata dict (168-177). fetch_openrouter_model_info (276-323) is the legacy scrape fallback. The class is the single indirection between aider and any metadata source, so it is the right seam to demonstrate the lookup path offline with a fixture cache.

Loads the local cache file only once per manager (_cache_loaded guard, 185-186) and only while cache_age < CACHE_TTL (191-192); a JSONDecodeError is treated exactly like a missing cache by resetting self.content to None (195-197). This is what makes a hand-written local fixture file a sufficient stand-in for the network: a fresh file is used verbatim, a stale or corrupted file simply falls through to _update_cache().

The primary lookup path. It first returns any in-memory local_model_metadata entry for the exact model name (224-226), then loads/refreshes the on-disk cache (229-232), then tries self.content.get(model) (237-239), and finally resolves 'provider/model' by looking up pieces[1] and accepting it only when its litellm_provider field equals pieces[0] (241-245). Every miss returns an empty dict (234-235, 247), never None and never an exception.

The fallback ladder. It calls get_model_from_cached_json_db, consults litellm.get_model_info only when litellm is already loaded or the cache missed (253-258, swallowing errors that mention the metadata file), prefers truthy litellm metadata (260-261), and for openrouter/* models additionally tries the cached OpenRouter db then the legacy web scrape (263-272). If every source is unavailable the function returns the empty cached_info dict (274). This is the documented 'metadata unavailable' behaviour demonstrated by the fixture demo.

The Model-facing entry point: Model.get_model_info delegates verbatim to the module-level model_info_manager singleton (instantiated at line 326), which Model.__init__ calls at line 348 to populate self.info and to derive max_chat_history_tokens (348-358). The demo swaps that singleton for a fixture-cache manager and shows the same metadata arriving on a real Model instance.

The repository's public contract for the unavailable-metadata fallback: constructing a real ModelInfoManager and calling get_model_info('non-existent-model') must return exactly {} (assertEqual(info, {})). The demo reproduces this contract (case 6a) without network access by answering the litellm stand-in with the same 'model_prices_and_context_window.json' error that real litellm raises for unknown models.

The companion contract for the successful lookup path: Model(name).info['max_input_tokens'] must come back from the metadata lookup with exact values (16385 for gpt-3.5-turbo/gpt-3.5-turbo-16k/gpt-3.5-turbo-1106, 8*1024 for gpt-4/gpt-4-0613). The demo asserts the same shape against the local fixture cache (cases 1a and 9a) and shows the derived max_chat_history_tokens (9b).

claims.claim: A fresh local cache file is authoritative: ModelInfoManager.get_model_from_cached_json_db returns the fixture entry for an exact model name and for 'provider/model' when pieces[1] exists and its litellm_provider equals the prefix, and it performs no network refresh and does not even load litellm when the cache hits (demo cases 1a-1c, 3a, 3c).

In-memory local_model_metadata is consulted before any file or network access, so it can seed metadata for a model with no cache file present (demo case 2a with a recorder showing zero cache/network calls).

When metadata is unavailable the lookup path degrades to an empty dict instead of raising: a corrupted cache file is treated as missing, a refresh that yields nothing leaves content empty, and get_model_info('non-existent-model') returns {} exactly as tests/basic/test_models.py test_get_model_info_nonexistent asserts (demo cases 4a-4c, 6a, 6b).

tests/basic/test_models.py is the public acceptance contract for this path: test_get_model_info_nonexistent pins the empty-dict fallback and test_max_context_tokens pins concrete max_input_tokens values surfaced through Model.info, so the demo's fixture-cache values are asserted in that same dict shape (info['max_input_tokens']).

Staleness is bounded and recoverable: a cache file older than CACHE_TTL (24h) is ignored and _update_cache() is invoked exactly once, after which the refreshed content serves the lookup (demo cases 5a, 5b).

Model-level consumers see the same lookup path: Model.get_model_info delegates to the module-level model_info_manager singleton, Model.__init__ stores the result in self.info, and max_chat_history_tokens is derived from it (4096/16 -> 1024 in the demo), which is the behaviour test_max_context_tokens checks for other models (demo cases 9a, 9b).

The full fallback ladder is deterministic and ordered: cache -> litellm (only when loaded or the cache missed, its truthy result preferred) -> cached OpenRouter db -> legacy OpenRouter scrape -> empty dict. The demo exercises each rung, including OpenRouter cases where the cached db answers, where only the scrape answers, and where neither does (demo cases 7a, 8a-8c).

conclusion: The model-info lookup path is demonstrable fully offline. Using a local fixture cache at .prale-eval/fixtures/model_prices_and_context_window.json, .prale-eval/demo_model_info_lookup.py drives the unmodified aider.models.ModelInfoManager through 21 assertions: exact cache hits and provider-prefixed resolution come straight from the local file; in-memory local_model_metadata wins over the file; a stale cache triggers exactly one refresh and a corrupted cache is treated as missing; and when no source is available the path deliberately falls back to {} (mirroring tests/basic/test_models.py::TestModels.test_get_model_info_nonexistent), with litellm consulted opportunistically when the cache misses. All 21 checks pass and the script exits 0. The repository test suite could not be collected in this environment because the optional dependencies json5, litellm, oslex (and, for the wider suite, pexpect/grep_ast) are not installed and installation is out of scope; the demo therefore substitutes controlled stand-ins in sys.modules for those imports, leaving repository sources, package locks and git configuration untouched.
